To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Early Jurassic coal forming deltaic coastal plain of the Mecsek area was characterised by plant succession stages related to the palaeotopographical features of the area.

(1) the palaeotopographic reconstruction of a coastal deltaic environment is based on the integration of coal seam ash content and isopach data; (2) plant succession stages were determined by palaeotopographical changes; (3) the peripheral zone of a delta is characterised by more dynamic plant changes than the central part.
“Palaeotopographically related plant succession stages were determined in a deltaic coastal plain environment of the Early Jurassic Mecsek Basin (SW Hungary).”
In summary, our research is concerned with

the palaeoecology of a delta plain environment, where the palaeogeographic position of the investigated area is of primary significance for the reconstruction of the vegetation and the palaeoenvironment.
the palaeotopographical and palaeogeographical reconstruction of the Early Jurassic deltaic succession based on the integration of sedimentological and paleobotanical data.
palaeotopographic and palaeoenvironmental changes during delta formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plant cover at the periphery of a deltaic coastal plain was less intensive and more dynamic than that of the central plain.
, based on palaeotopographic reconstruction and palaeobotany, the Mecsek Coal Formation represents the deltaic plain environment of the Early Jurassic Mecsek Basin.

the Early Jurassic deltaic plain of Mecsek Basin (Hungary) was characterised by a mosaic of habitats of different topography and water level, and the plant cover changed according to the environmental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the palaeotopographical changes in the delta plain environment were the most significant factor controlling the plant composition and succession stages in the studied area.
plant succession stages can be reconstructed based on palaeotopographical changes in the coal forming environment.
plant succession stages are useful to interpret the plant growing intensity and the palaeotopographic conditions in coal bearing deltaic environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
palaeotopographical changes can be detected from palaeobotanical assemblages in a deltaic succession.
plant communities can be used to detect palaeotopographic changes in the deltaic environment, thus they can be applied to reconstruct palaoecological conditions in the deltaic area.

the palaeobotanical record of the Early Jurassic coal-bearing succession of the Mecsek Coal Formation can be interpreted by a palaeoecologically-based model, which is based on the palaeotopographical reconstruction of the depositional environment.
